checks.derivation: On R4 let J be an orthogonal complex structure, g Euclidean and V=(-I+J)x/2. The complete flow is exp(-t/2)exp(tJ/2)x, and Ric+(LVg)/2+g/2=0. The proper end embedding iota(r,theta)=r exp(-log(r)J)theta/sqrt(2) gives gamma_rr=1, beta=-eta/2, h=h_round/2 and |beta|_h^2=1/2, with exact asymptotic equality and iota_*(-r partial_r/2)=V. The admissible tangent gamma'=gamma-dr^2 becomes T=I-2ee^T beyond the cutoff. Since nabla_V e=Je/2, nabla_V T=-[(Je)e^T+e(Je)^T] has constant squared norm 2. Thus the stated m=0 r^-2 bound fails with the fixed vector field and all standing end/topology hypotheses.
checks.assessment: Minor local overgenerality. Source Remark3.9 prevents replacing the specified non-gradient V with a different gradient field. The inspected Lemma8.11 application has a gradient base and hence an ordinary cone; no core theorem failure is shown.

checks.claim: Problem2: arbitrary analytic slices and dimension sum
checks.derivation: At the Gaussian cone take five independent small angular cone tensors and Q1=(x,y,0,0,0), Q2=(x,y,x^2,xy,y^2). Positivity, analyticity and orientation hold after shrinking; the slices need only intersect the nonnegative-scalar cone. The source Gaussian-fiber uniqueness and index-zero/kernel-zero statements give surjectivity at that fiber; Lemma10.31 supplies a neighborhood where full transversality holds. Any C2 common manifold has second fundamental form zero on the shared tangent E because Q1 is flat. The second derivatives of Q2 then force e3,e4,e5 into its tangent, as well as e1,e2: dimension at least five, contradicting the printed sum four.
checks.assessment: Minor false dimension bound on the degree-construction proof path. A five-dimensional affine containing slice works for this example; nested comparison uses finite containment, not that exact sum. No unequal degrees or false main theorem are established.

checks.derivation: For affine slices the sum of their direction spaces is a common finite-dimensional slice and can be shrunk using Lemma10.31. This does not prove arbitrary curved slices always admit the claimed finite common refinement.
